premises: Corrosion resistance in steels is governed by a uniform, stoichiometric, Cr-rich passive oxide layer.
Electrochemical surface pre-treatment enhances formation and adherence of this protective layer in austenitic stainless steels.
An optimized Cr:Mo ratio facilitates a robust, self-healing passive film in Fe–Cr–Mo steels under high-temperature, high-pressure conditions.
Improved surface finish minimizes defects and promotes uniform oxide formation.
